 Illinois expands walk-in DMV services for veterans, active-duty military
 Published 4:25 pm Thursday, November 5, 2026
 By STAFF REPORT 
 Illinois Secretary of State 
 Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... 
 CHICAGO — Illinois Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias has permanently opened the state’s four Senior-Only DMV locations to veterans and active-duty military personnel, who can now be served there without an appointment.
 Giannoulias announced the change in recognition of National Veterans and Military Families Month. Veterans and service members may visit any of the four sites Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. to obtain driver’s licenses, REAL IDs, vehicle registrations, and other services. The locations are the Evanston Senior Center, 300 Dodge Ave.; the Bridgeview Senior Center, 7900 S. Oketo Ave.; the Westchester Senior Center, 10300 W. Roosevelt Road; and the Calumet Park Senior Center, 12633 S. Ashland Ave.
 Visitors must present documentation verifying their military status. For veterans, accepted items include an Illinois driver’s license or state ID with a veteran designation, a DD214 discharge form, a Veteran Health Identification Card, or a Department of Defense ID card. Active-duty personnel can show a Common Access Card, a military pay stub, reserve activation orders, an enlistment contract, or an official statement of service, among other documents.
 “Our veterans and military service members have dedicated themselves to protecting our country,” Giannoulias said in a statement. “Making it easier for them to access essential government services is a small but meaningful way we can serve them in return.”
 The Senior-Only DMVs offer walk-in driver and vehicle services, including license applications and renewals, REAL ID applications, title and registration services, driving tests, disability parking placards, and license plate sticker renewals.
 The expansion was made possible by the Road Safety & Fairness Act, which took effect July 1. The law eliminated mandatory driving tests for drivers ages 79 to 86, reducing demand for testing at senior-focused facilities and freeing capacity to serve more people while keeping access convenient for seniors, according to the Secretary of State’s office.
 Veterans groups welcomed the move. Megan Everett, executive director of Illinois Joining Forces, called appointment-free service “a welcome step toward making everyday services easier to access.” The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs said it is partnering with the Secretary of State’s office and the Jesse Brown VA Medical Center in Chicago to expand access for veterans and military families.
 The Secretary of State’s office also offers other benefits to military families. Veterans can add a “VETERAN” designation to a driver’s license or ID card, and active-duty members and eligible spouses and children can get a free duplicate license or ID. Illinois offers 46 specialized military license plates, and veterans can switch to a military plate free of charge, though vanity and personalized plates carry additional fees. Veterans with a service-connected disability of 50% or greater may qualify for one set of military plates without a registration fee. Eligible active-duty members and reservists returning from combat missions may qualify for a waiver of their standard registration fee.
 The office also maintains the Illinois Veterans’ History Project, which has more than 6,700 records, including 675 oral histories.
